name: Banh khoai
summary: A turmeric rice-flour crepe, pan-fried until it crunches, with shrimp, quail egg, bean sprouts, and pork belly.
origin: Hue. Vietnam Tourism places the crepe on Kim Long.
history: Vietnam Tourism groups bánh khoái with the Hue dishes it ties to the Nguyen court kitchens.
culture: It is the crepe on the north-bank road toward Thien Mu, eaten with a fresh salad and a thick sauce.
texture: Vietnam Tourism calls it a crunch: a pan-fried rice-flour crepe turned yellow with turmeric, folded over shrimp, a quail egg, bean sprouts, and pork belly.
taste: The sauce is peanuts and pork liver. A salad of fig, starfruit, and cucumber is there to cut the grease.
howToEat: Eat it folded, with the salad and the sauce.
where: Kim Long, on the way toward Thien Mu. The hour is check on arrival.
seoTitle: Banh khoai in Hue — the turmeric crepe on Kim Long
seoDescription: A crunchy turmeric crepe with shrimp, pork, and a peanut-and-liver sauce, along Kim Long toward Thien Mu. A stall price is check on arrival.
